segments.arabic:
١١٢٧٢- زينب الأحمسية
ذكرها أبو سعيد بن الأعرابيّ، وأبو محمّد بن حزم
في كتابي حجّة الوداع، من طريقه بسند له عن زينب الأحمسية- أن رسول اللَّه ﷺ قال لها في امرأة حجّت معها مصمتة «قولي لها تتكلّم، فإنّه لا حجّ لمن لا يتكلّم»،
وقد طعن فيه ابن القطان أن في سنده مجهولين، وفي سياقه غلط.
والصواب ما تقدم في القسم قبله أن القصة جرت لزينب مع أبي بكر الصديق، والمخاطبة بينهما باللفظ الّذي تقدم لا ذكر للنّبيّ ﷺ فيه ولا لامرأة أخرى.
segments.english:
11272 — Zaynab al-Ahmasiyya

Abu Sa'id ibn al-A'rabi and Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm mentioned her in their two books entitled The Farewell Pilgrimage, through his route, with an isnad of his from Zaynab al-Ahmasiyya: the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to her concerning a woman who performed the pilgrimage with her while keeping silent: “Tell her to speak, for there is no pilgrimage for one who does not speak.”

Ibn al-Qattan criticized it because its isnad contains two unknown transmitters and its wording contains an error.

The correct account is what was stated above in the preceding section: the incident took place between Zaynab and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and the exchange between them used the wording given above; it contains no mention of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or of another woman.

unresolved.explanation: The singular pronouns do not unambiguously identify which of the two previously named authors supplied the route and isnad. The English preserves that ambiguity.
